meta.title: Directive 2010/64/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 October 2010 on the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings

items.heading: Article 1

nationalActs.title: Ley Orgánica 5/2015, de 27 de abril, por la que se modifican la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal y la Ley Orgánica 6/1985, de 1 de julio, del Poder Judicial, para transponer la Directiva 2010/64/UE, de 20 de octubre de 2010, relativa al derecho a interpretación y a traducción en los procesos penales y la Directiva 2012/13/UE, de 22 de mayo de 2012, relativa al derecho a la información en los procesos penales
nationalActs.titleEn: Organic Law 5/2015, of April 27, amending the Criminal Procedural Law and Organic Law 6/1985, of July 1, of the Judiciary, to transpose Directive 2010/64 / EU, of 20 of October 2010, regarding the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings and Directive 2012/13 / EU, of May 22, 2012, concerning the right to information in criminal proceedings

items.comment:
This Directive has been explicitly transposed by the Organic Law 5/2015, of April 27, amending the Criminal Procedural Law and the Organic Law 6/1985, of July 1, of the Judiciary, to transpose Directive 2010/64 / EU, of 20 of October 2010, regarding the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings and Directive 2012/13 / EU, of May 22, 2012, concerning the right to information in criminal proceedings.


Therefore, in the analysis of the following articles, reference will be made to the amended laws. Specifically, reference will be made to the Criminal Procedural Law and the Organic Law of the Judiciary.

items.text: 1. This Directive lays down rules concerning the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings and proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant.

2. The right referred to in paragraph 1 shall apply to persons from the time that they are made aware by the competent authorities of a Member State, by official notification or otherwise, that they are suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence until the conclusion of the proceedings, which is understood to mean the final determination of the question whether they have committed the offence, including, where applicable, sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: The aforementioned legislation states the momento from which the right is applicable, but it states nothing regarding about until what procedural moment the right will be recognized. Therefore is not expressly stated that the right shall be recognized until the conclusion of the proceedings, including sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.
provisions.textEn: “Any person to whom a punishable act is attributed may exercise the right of defense, intervening in the proceedings, since its existence is communicated, has been subject to detention or any other precautionary measure or has been indicted, for which, s/he will be informed, without undue delay, of the following rights: (…) f) The right to free translation and interpretation in accordance with the provisions of articles 123 and 127"

items.text: 3. Where the law of a Member State provides for the imposition of a sanction regarding minor offences by an authority other than a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters, and the imposition of such a sanction may be appealed to such a court, this Directive shall apply only to the proceedings before that court following such an appeal.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: In Spain, penal sanctions for minor offences are always imposed by Courts having jurisdiction in criminal matters, therefore this provision is not applicable.

items.text: 4. This Directive does not affect national law concerning the presence of legal counsel during any stage of the criminal proceedings, nor does it affect national law concerning the right of access of a suspected or accused person to documents in criminal proceedings.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspected or accused persons who do not speak or understand the language of the criminal proceedings concerned are provided, without delay, with interpretation during criminal proceedings before investigative and judicial authorities, including during police questioning, all court hearings and any necessary interim hearings.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: Those defendants who do not speak or understand Spanish or the official language in which the action takes place shall have the following rights: a) Right to be assisted by an interpreter who uses a language that s/he understands during all the proceedings in which his/her presence is necessary, including police interrogation or by the Prosecutor's Office and all judicial hearings.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that, where necessary for the purpose of safeguarding the fairness of the proceedings, interpretation is available for communication between suspected or accused persons and their legal counsel in direct connection with any questioning or hearing during the proceedings or with the lodging of an appeal or other procedural applications.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn:
Defendants or accused persons who do not speak or understand Spanish or the official language in which the proceedings are taking place shall have the following rights: (...)


b) The right to have an interpreter in the conversations that s/he has with his/her lawyer and that are directly related to his/her subsequent interrogation or declaration, or that are necessary for the presentation of an appeal or for other procedural requests.

provisions.comment: This provision extends the scope of the right to other procedural acts. In general, any proceedings involving the accused and his or her counsel will require the assistance of an interpreter, as otherwise their rights of defence may be affected. The interpreter must intervene so that the suspect can be informed and advised on the obligation to collaborate in the carrying out of the proceedings, on the consequences of his refusal to collaborate or, in general, on his rights. E.g. collection of DNA samples, reconstruction of facts, identity parades, etc.
provisions.textEn:
Defendants or accused persons who do not speak or understand Spanish or the official language in which the proceedings are taking place shall have the following rights:


(a) The right to be assisted by an interpreter during all proceedings in which his presence is required, including police or prosecutorial questioning and all court hearings

provisions.comment: This provision extends the scope of the right to the trial
provisions.textEn:
Defendants or accused persons who do not speak or understand Spanish or the official language in which the proceedings are taking place shall have the following rights: (...)


(c) The right to interpretation of all proceedings in the trial

items.text: 3. The right to interpretation under paragraphs 1 and 2 includes appropriate assistance for persons with hearing or speech impediments.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: The provisions contained in the preceding articles are equally applicable to people with sensory disabilities, who shall have available means of support for oral communication.

items.text: 4. Member States shall ensure that a procedure or mechanism is in place to ascertain whether suspected or accused persons speak and understand the language of the criminal proceedings and whether they need the assistance of an interpreter.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: The article is too indeterminate, there is no indication of what the evaluation process will consist of, who will carry it out and under what circumstances the evaluation will be initiated.
provisions.textEn: When the need for assistance of an interpreter or translator arises from the circumstances, the President of the Court or the Judge, ex officio or at the request of the Defense Attorney, shall ascertain whether the defendant knows and understands sufficiently the official language in which proceedings are being carried out and, where appropriate, shall order the appointment of an interpreter or a translator in accordance with the provisions of the previous article and preceding Article and shall determine which documents must be translated.

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with procedures in national law, suspected or accused persons have the right to challenge a decision finding that there is no need for interpretation and, when interpretation has been provided, the possibility to complain that the quality of the interpretation is not sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: The referral made to the general system of resources does not fully respond to the requirements of this article of the Directive, since it is not clarified how to proceed when the denial comes from the Police or the Posecutor, whose resolutions are not directly appealable.
provisions.textEn:
The decision of the Judge or Court that denies the right to interpretation or translation of any document or passage thereof that the defense considers essential, or by which the complaints of the defense in relation to lack of quality of the interpretation or translation are rejected, will be documented in writing.

If the decision had been taken during the trial, the defense of the accused may ask for the record of his/her protest in the minutes.

An appeal may be lodged against these judicial decisions in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

items.text: 6. Where appropriate, communication technology such as videoconferencing, telephone or the Internet may be used, unless the physical presence of the interpreter is required in order to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: There is a certain inversion of the general rule, which becomes telematic communication with the interpreter, with physical presence being exceptional.
provisions.textEn: The assistance of the interpreter may be provided through videoconference or by any means of telecommunication, unless the Court or the Judge or the Public Prosecutor, ex officio or at the request of the interested party or his/her defense lawyer, agrees the physical presence of the interpreter in order to safeguard the rights of the accused.

items.text: 7. In proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant, the executing Member State shall ensure that its competent authorities provide persons subject to such proceedings who do not speak or understand the language of the proceedings with interpretation in accordance with this Article.

nationalActs.title: Ley 23/2014, de 20 de noviembre, de reconocimiento mutuo de resoluciones penales en la Unión Europea
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on mutual recognition of criminal decisions in the European Union

provisions.textEn: The hearing of the arrested person shall be held within a maximum period of seventy-two hours after being brought to justice, with the assistance of the Prosecutor, the lawyer of the detained person and, where appropriate, an interpreter, and must be carried out in accordance with provided for the questioning of the person detained by the Criminal Procedure Act

items.text: 8. Interpretation provided under this Article shall be of a quality sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, in particular by ensuring that suspected or accused persons have knowledge of the case against them and are able to exercise their right of defence.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: When the Court, the Judge or the Public Prosecutor's Office, ex officio or at the request of a party, appreciates that the translation or interpretation does not offer sufficient guarantees of accuracy, they may order the conduction of the necessary checks and, where appropriate, it may be ordered the designation of a new translator or interpreter. In this sense, deaf or hearing impaired people who appreciate that the interpretation does not offer sufficient guarantees of accuracy, may request the appointment of a new interpreter.

items.heading: Article 3
items.subHeading: Right to translation of essential documents

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspected or accused persons who do not understand the language of the criminal proceedings concerned are, within a reasonable period of time, provided with a written translation of all documents which are essential to ensure that they are able to exercise their right of defence and to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn:
Defendants who do not speak or understand Spanish or the official language in which the action takes place will have the following rights (...):

d) Right to the written translation of the documents that are essential to guarantee the exercise of the right to defense. Decision on depirivation of liberty of the accused, the indictment and the sentence must be always translated.

The translation must be carried out within a reasonable period of time and the applicable procedural deadlines shall be suspended as soon as the translation is ordered by the Court, Judge or Public Prosecutor's Office

items.text: 2. Essential documents shall include any decision depriving a person of his liberty, any charge or indictment, and any judgment.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn:
1. Defendants or accused persons who do not speak or understand Spanish or the official language in which the proceedings are taking place shall have the following rights

(d) the right to written translation of documents which are essential for the exercise of the right of defence. In any event, the decisions ordering the detention of the accused, the indictment and the judgment must be translated.

items.text: 3. The competent authorities shall, in any given case, decide whether any other document is essential. Suspected or accused persons or their legal counsel may submit a reasoned request to that effect.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: When the need for the assistance of an interpreter or translator arise from the circumstances of the case, the President of the Court or the Judge, ex officio or at the request of the Defense Attorney or the accused, shall verify whether s/he knows and understands sufficiently the official language in which the procedure is carried out and, where appropriate, will order the appointment of an interpreter or translator in accordance with the provisions of the previous article and will determine which documents should be translated.

Defendants who do not speak or understand Spanish or the official language in which the procedure are taking place will have the following rights: (...) e) the right to submit a reasoned request for a document to be considered essential.

Defendants or accused persons who do not speak or understand Spanish or the official language in which the proceedings are taking place shall have the following rights: (...)

(d) the right to written translation of documents which are essential for the exercise of the right of defence. In any event, the decisions ordering the detention of the accused, the indictment and the judgment must be translated.

items.text: 4. There shall be no requirement to translate passages of essential documents which are not relevant for the purposes of enabling suspected or accused persons to have knowledge of the case against them.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: In the case of paragraph 1(d), the translation of the passages of the essential documents that, at the discretion of the Judge, Court or competent civil servant are not necessary for the knowledge of the facts by the accused or defendant shall be dispensable.

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with procedures in national law, suspected or accused persons have the right to challenge a decision finding that there is no need for the translation of documents or passages thereof and, when a translation has been provided, the possibility to complain that the quality of the translation is not sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn:
The decision of the Judge or Court that denies the right to interpretation or translation of any document or passage thereof that the defense considers essential, or by which the complaints of the defense in relation to lack of quality of the interpretation or translation are rejected, will be documented in writing.

If the decision had been taken during the trial, the defense of the accused may ask for the record of his/her protest in the minutes.

An appeal may be lodged against these judicial decisions in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

items.text: 6. In proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant, the executing Member State shall ensure that its competent authorities provide any person subject to such proceedings who does not understand the language in which the European arrest warrant is drawn up, or into which it has been translated by the issuing Member State, with a written translation of that document.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Although there is no express provision in this regard in the Law on mutual recognition of criminal decisions in the European Union, taking into account the need to translate the essential documents of the criminal procedure, it may be understood that the arrest warrant is one of those essential documents.

items.text: 7. As an exception to the general rules established in paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 6, an oral translation or oral summary of essential documents may be provided instead of a written translation on condition that such oral translation or oral summary does not prejudice the fairness of the proceedings.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: Exceptionally, the written translation of documents may be replaced by an oral summary of their content in a language that the defendant understands, provided that the right of defense of the accused is sufficiently guaranteed also in this way.

items.text: 8. Any waiver of the right to translation of documents referred to in this Article shall be subject to the requirements that suspected or accused persons have received prior legal advice or have otherwise obtained full knowledge of the consequences of such a waiver, and that the waiver was unequivocal and given voluntarily.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: The waiver of the rights referred to in article 123 must be express and free, and will only be valid if it occurs after the accused has received sufficient and accessible legal advice to enable him/her to become aware of the consequences of his renunciation. In any event, the rights referred to in Article 123(1)(a) and (c) may not be waived.

items.text: 9. Translation provided under this Article shall be of a quality sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, in particular by ensuring that suspected or accused persons have knowledge of the case against them and are able to exercise their right of defence.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Although there is no express provision in this regard, it is understood implicitly in the essential content of the right, as well as in the possibility of the defense of making complaints regarding the lack of quality of interpretation or translation

items.text: Member States shall meet the costs of interpretation and translation resulting from the application of Articles 2 and 3, irrespective of the outcome of the proceedings.
items.heading: Article 4

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: Translation and interpretation expenses arising from the exercise of these rights will be paid by the Administration, regardless of the outcome of the procedure.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Quality of the interpretation and translation

items.text: 1. Member States shall take concrete measures to ensure that the interpretation and translation provided meets the quality required under Article 2(8) and Article 3(9).

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: When the Court, the Judge or the Public Prosecutor's Office, ex officio or at the request of a party, appreciates that the translation or interpretation does not offer sufficient guarantees of accuracy, it may order the conduction of the necessary checks and, where appropriate, he designation of a new translator or interpreter may be ordered. In this sense, deaf or hearing impaired people who appreciate that the interpretation does not offer sufficient guarantees of accuracy, may request the appointment of a new interpreter.

items.text: 2. In order to promote the adequacy of interpretation and translation and efficient access thereto, Member States shall endeavour to establish a register or registers of independent translators and interpreters who are appropriately qualified. Once established, such register or registers shall, where appropriate, be made available to legal counsel and relevant authorities.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment:
The possibility provided by Spanish law for cases of emergency consisting of enabling anyone who knows the language as an interpreter, without determining which are those urgent cases that allow the use of an untitled interpreter, may be detrimental to the quality of the service.


An Official Registry of qualified interpreters and translators has not been created yet. In addition is questionable the fact that the Spanish law is limited to refer the existence of a list prepared by the Administration, without specifying the training requirements for being on such list.
provisions.textEn: The court translator or interpreter shall be appointed from among those included in the lists drawn up by the competent Administration. Exceptionally, in those cases that require the urgent presence of a translator or interpreter, and the intervention of a court translator or interpreter registered on the lists drawn up by the Administration is not possible, in accordance with the provisions of section 5 of the previous article, another person with knowledge of the language used who is considered qualified to carry out the assignment may be appointed

nationalActs.title: Ley Orgánica 5/2015, de 27 de abril, por la que se modifican la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal y la Ley Orgánica 6/1985, de 1 de julio, del Poder Judicial, para transponer la Directiva 2010/64/UE, de 20 de octubre de 2010, relativa al derecho a interpretación y a traducción en los procesos penales y la Directiva 2012/13/UE, de 22 de mayo de 2012, relativa al derecho a la información en los procesos penales
nationalActs.titleEn: Organic Law 5/2015, of April 27, amending the Criminal Procedural Law and Organic Law 6/1985, of July 1, of the Judiciary, to transpose Directive 2010/64 / EU, of 20 of October 2010, regarding the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings and Directive 2012/13 / EU, of May 22, 2012, concerning the right to information in criminal proceedings

provisions.comment: Despite the fact that the one-year deadline for the creation of the Registry expired on 25 April 2016, the Draft Act establishing it has not yet been submitted.
provisions.textEn: The Government shall submit, within a maximum of one year from the publication of this Act, a bill for the creation of an Official Registry of Court Translators and Interpreters for the registration of all those professionals who are duly authorized and qualified, in order to draw up the lists of translators and interpreters referred to in Article 124 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Registration in this Official Register will be a necessary requirement for the actions of these professionals by appointment of the Judge or the Judicial Secretary before the Administration of Justice and in the police proceedings in which their presence is necessary, without prejudice to the exceptions established. For the purposes of registration in this Official Register, the Ministry of Justice may request compliance with other requirements different from the training or qualifications that are established by regulation according to the language in question. These requirements must be proportionate and non-discriminatory and may be based on the experience of the professional, on additional knowledge of procedural or legal matters, and on compliance with deontological duties provided for by law.

items.text: 3. Member States shall ensure that interpreters and translators be required to observe confidentiality regarding interpretation and translation provided under this Directive.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: The designated interpreter or translator must respect the confidential nature of the service provided.

The translators and interpreters of the conversations and communications with the defendant are exempt from the obligation to declare in relation to the facts to which their translation or interpretation was referred.

items.text: Without prejudice to judicial independence and differences in the organisation of the judiciary across the Union, Member States shall request those responsible for the training of judges, prosecutors and judicial staff involved in criminal proceedings to pay special attention to the particularities of communicating with the assistance of an interpreter so as to ensure efficient and effective communication.
items.heading: Article 6

nationalActs.title: Ley 27/2007, de 23 de octubre, por la que se reconocen las lenguas de signos españolas y se regulan los medios de apoyo a la comunicación oral de las personas sordas, con discapacidad auditiva y sordociegas
nationalActs.titleEn: Law 27/2007, of October 23, by which Spanish sign languages are recognized, and speech communication aids for the deaf, hard of hearing and deafblind, are regulated

provisions.comment: The provision does not refer to foreign language interpreters, it is limited only to training related to the communication of deaf, hard of hearing and deafblind persons.
provisions.textEn: The Public Administration shall promote the appropriate conditions, such as training in and availability of speech communication aids, to facilitate relations of deaf, hard of hearing and deafblind persons with the Public Administration. In regard to the Justice Administration, adequate conditions, such as training in and availability of speech communication aids, shall be promoted in order to put into practice the stipulations of Article 143 of the Civil Procedural Law, as well as in procedures governed by the Criminal Prosecution Law regarding deaf, hard of hearing and deafblind.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that when a suspected or accused person has been subject to questioning or hearings by an investigative or judicial authority with the assistance of an interpreter pursuant to Article 2, when an oral translation or oral summary of essential documents has been provided in the presence of such an authority pursuant to Article 3(7), or when a person has waived the right to translation pursuant to Article 3(8), it will be noted that these events have occurred, using the recording procedure in accordance with the law of the Member State concerned.
items.heading: Article 7

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: Article 126 of the Criminal Procedural Law regulates the possibility of waiving certain rights related to translation, but does not expressly refer to the need to record such renounciation.
provisions.textEn: Oral or sign language interpretations, other than those provided for in paragraph 1(b), may be documented by means of the audiovisual recording of the original event and the interpretation. In cases of oral or sign language translation of the content of a document, a copy of the translated document and the audiovisual recording of the translation shall be attached to the minutes. If recording equipment is not available, or is not deemed appropriate or necessary, the translation or interpretation and, where appropriate, the original statement shall be documented in writing.
